title: What Are Popcorn Buds? Small Nugs, Real Value
h1: Popcorn Buds Explained: What They Are and Whether They're Worth It
metaDescription: Popcorn buds are small flowers from lower on the plant. Learn why they cost less, how they compare, how to pick a strain and what the label shows.
excerpt: Popcorn buds are the small nugs from lower on the plant. Here is why they cost less, when they are a smart buy and what to check before you pick some up.

body:
Popcorn buds are the small, rounded flowers that grow on a cannabis plant's lower branches. They come from the same plants as the big top buds, just smaller and less showy, which is why they usually cost less. Whether they're worth it depends on how you'll use them and what the label says.

## What popcorn buds are

Cannabis flowers form all along a plant's branches. Big, dense buds tend to develop near the top, where light is strongest, while lower flowers get less light and stay smaller.

Growers sort these small buds out and sell them on their own, often as "popcorn" or "small buds," a name that fits their size. Our tour of [cannabis plant anatomy](/blog/anatomy-of-cannabis-plant-from-seed-to-bud/) shows where each kind of bud forms.

## Why popcorn buds cost less

Mostly, it's about looks. Big buds fill a jar and catch the eye, so they sell for more, even when small buds come from the same harvest.

Potency is a separate question. Greenhouse research has found that buds at the bottom of the plant can carry lower cannabinoid levels than the top bud. In one study, some lower buds tested up to 90% lower.

Pruning and extra light in the lower canopy narrowed those gaps in other studies, so popcorn from one grower may test close to its top buds while another's may not. The label matters more than bud size.

## The upside: price, same strain, ready to grind

- **Lower cost per gram,** which makes popcorn a natural budget cannabis flower option.
- **The same strain,** so you get its familiar aroma profile, though intensity can vary.
- **Easy to grind** for joints, bowls or a dry-herb vaporizer.
- **Low-stakes sampling** when you want to try a new strain.

## Popcorn buds vs. regular buds: when each makes sense

| What you want | Popcorn buds | Full-size buds |
|---|---|---|
| Lower cost per gram | Usually the better fit | Usually priced higher |
| Rolling or packing bowls | Grinds fast | Works, with more breaking up |
| A showpiece jar | Less eye-catching | Dense, photogenic buds |
| Predictable potency | Check each label | Check each label |

Our comparison of [buds, shake and popcorn nugs](/blog/cannabis-bud-vs-shake-vs-popcorn/) adds shake to the mix.

## Choosing a strain: terpene and type cues

Pick popcorn buds the way you'd pick any flower. Aroma is a good starting point, since citrus, pine, pepper and earthy notes come from terpenes. If you liked a strain's full-size buds, its popcorn is a natural next try.

Indica, sativa and hybrid labels are loose hints. The THC number, terpene details where listed and your own notes tell you more. Our budtenders can help you look for small buds with a profile you already like.

## Checking lab results and the harvest date

Michigan requires every cannabis package to list THC and CBD content, with a note that actual values may vary by 10%. Labels must also show the harvest date, the testing lab and the test date.

Some packages also show a packaging date, but the harvest date is the one Michigan requires, and it says more about freshness. Aroma fades in storage, so fresher flower tends to smell brighter. Our guide to [reading a cannabis label](/blog/how-to-read-a-cannabis-label/) walks through every line.

## Storage tips for small buds

- Keep them in an airtight glass jar, somewhere cool and dark.
- Keep them away from heat and sunlight, which speed up THC breakdown.
- Grind just before use. In storage research, ground flower lost aroma compounds faster than whole flower.

For the full routine, see [how to store cannabis](/blog/how-to-store-marijuana/).

Mostly because of size and looks. Small buds don't fill a jar or catch the eye the way big, dense buds do, so they usually sell for less per gram. They come from the same plants, so check the THC and harvest date rather than judging by size.

faq.q: Are popcorn buds good for joints?
faq.a: Yes. Small buds grind quickly and evenly, which makes them practical for rolling joints or packing bowls. Grind them just before you roll, since ground flower loses aroma faster than whole buds. New to a strain? Start with a small amount.

faq.q: How do I check lab results on flower?
faq.a: Start with the label. In Michigan, every package must list THC and CBD content, the harvest date, the testing lab and the test date. For more detail, ask a budtender what testing information is available, or look up the producer, since some publish fuller lab reports.

claims.claim: Popcorn buds are small flowers from a plant's lower branches, from the same plants as the top buds
claims.source: Common trade definition; consistent with Danziger and Bernstein 2021 Plants abstract, PMID 34579367 (E-utilities) (bottom inflorescences get less light)

claims.claim: Big, dense buds develop near the top where light is strongest; lower flowers get less light and stay smaller
claims.source: Danziger and Bernstein 2021 Plants abstract, PMID 34579367 (E-utilities): "low cannabinoid concentrations in inflorescences at the bottom of the plants correlate with low light penetration"; Danziger and Bernstein 2022 Front Plant Sci abstract, PMID 36247643 (E-utilities) (chronic light deprivation at the bottom)

claims.claim: Greenhouse research found bottom buds can carry lower cannabinoid levels than the top bud; in one study some tested up to 90% lower
